walkthroughs.body_html:
A force is simply a push or a pull. You can't see forces, but you can see what they do.

Forces are measured in newtons (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton. A small apple weighs about 1 N.

Forces can make things start moving, stop moving, speed up, slow down, or change direction.

Contact forces only work when things touch. Examples: friction, air resistance, tension in a rope.

Non-contact forces act across a gap. The three main ones are gravity, magnetism, and electrostatic forces.

The Moon pulls Earth's oceans without touching them - that's gravity at work!

People mix these up, but they're different!

Mass = how much stuff is in you. It stays the same everywhere (kg).

Weight = the pull of gravity on your mass. It changes on different planets (N).

On the Moon, your mass is the same, but your weight is about 1/6 of Earth's!

mcqs.q: Which has the longer wavelength: microwaves or radio waves?
options: Radio waves — they sit at the longest-wavelength end of the EM spectrum.
They have the same wavelength because both are used for communication.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
Microwaves, because they are used in 'big' devices like radar.

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.
They have the same wavelength because both are used for communication.

mcqs.q: How does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity?
options: Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
Higher intensity gives photoelectrons more kinetic energy.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
It does not — max KE depends only on the frequency of the light; intensity affects the rate (number) of electrons emitted.
